issues.description: Duplicate "transcriber_error" in the message_type tuple — sloppy copy-paste.
issues.detail: The tuple lists "transcriber_error" twice. It's harmless at runtime but it's the kind of thing that tells me the author didn't reread their own diff. If you can't keep a 14-item list deduplicated, what else got past you? Drop the duplicate before this lands.

issues.description: push_error gets the raw upstream string and loses the message_type context for non-generic errors.
issues.detail: Old code prefixed "Auth error:" and "Quota exceeded:" so downstream consumers and logs could distinguish them. New code collapses everything to "Error: <error>". You also dropped the per-type logger.error call. If the goal was uniform handling, fine — but include message_type in the pushed error so an auth_error doesn't look like a transient rate_limited.

issues.description: Rename of _process_messages to _receive_messages collapses two methods but the commit message doesn't say so.
issues.detail: This is THREE-PATCHES territory: (1) fix the infinite-loop by removing the swallowing try/except, (2) rename/merge the helper, (3) expand error message_type coverage. Squashed into one diff with a two-line changelog. The rename in particular is invisible to anyone scanning history for the infinite-loop fix. Split it, or at least call it out.

"\ No newline at end of file" on a new file you just created. Trivial, but it's the kind of thing the maintainer six months from now notices when their editor reflows it and produces a noisy diff. Add the newline.

issues.description: Good taste: collapsing three near-identical elif branches into a tuple membership test is the right move.
issues.detail: This is the correct shape. Three branches that did the same thing with different strings became one branch with a list of strings. That's the elimination of special cases — GOOD-TASTE. Just clean up the duplicate entry and preserve the type context in the pushed error and it lands.

review.summary: NEEDS-WORK. The core fix is right: the old _receive_messages swallowed every exception from the async-for loop, so a disconnected websocket got logged-and-forgotten instead of letting the outer reconnect loop run. Removing that try/except and letting the exception propagate is the correct shape. The error-type expansion is also the right refactor — three special cases collapsed into one general case is good taste. But the diff ships with a duplicate \"transcriber_error\" entry, drops the per-type prefix in the pushed error (auth vs quota now indistinguishable downstream), and bundles a silent rename with the bugfix. Fix the dup, preserve message_type in the error frame, and it lands.
